LoloBuy parcel status not updating: what should you check?

How to read each parcel stage, verify the waybill and send support the evidence needed to investigate.

⌕

Tracking & support · 10 minute read

LoloBuy parcel status not updating: a practical support guide

A LoloBuy parcel status that has not changed does not automatically mean the shipment is lost. The account shows two related but different records: the parcel’s workflow status and the carrier-facing logistics events. One can change before the other. The useful first step is therefore not to refresh several tracking sites, but to identify which record is actually unchanged and what evidence the parcel page currently provides.

The current LoloBuy interface labels parcel workflow stages as Pending payment, Processing, Risk control, Shipped, Canceled and Completed. Package Details can separately show a package number, waybill number, shipping method, recipient, item list and Tracking & logistics section. This guide explains how to read those fields, document a genuine gap and contact support without inventing a delivery deadline or assuming an outcome.

1. Start with the correct number

Keep the product order, international parcel and carrier waybill separate. A product order follows goods from purchase to the LoloBuy warehouse. A package number identifies the international parcel created from one or more stored items. A waybill number identifies the shipment within the logistics network after one is assigned. These references may appear together, but they are not interchangeable.

Open My Packages and select the relevant parcel rather than searching with a product title. In Package Details, record the package number, parcel status, shipping method, destination country and waybill number if one is displayed. Then compare the item list with the goods you submitted. This prevents a support request about one parcel from being attached to an unrelated order.

If no waybill number is shown, the parcel may not yet have reached the carrier-tracking stage. If a waybill exists, copy it exactly, including letters and leading zeroes. Do not publish any of these numbers in a public review; send them only through the appropriate private support channel.

2. Read the parcel workflow status before reading the scans

Pending payment means the parcel payment step is not complete in the account. Check the parcel record and related bill before expecting packing or shipment activity. Do not retry blindly if a payment appears on your bank side but the LoloBuy record is unclear; preserve the transaction reference and confirm the status first.

Processing is an internal parcel stage. The warehouse may still be handling packing, final weight or another operational step. It is not the same as a carrier scan. Review the parcel details and site messages for a request involving an amount due, address, item restriction or other action.

Risk control is also a parcel-level status, not proof that customs has detained the shipment. Treat it as a reason to check private account messages and ask what information or action is required. Do not guess at the cause or submit altered product information.

Shipped means the parcel has moved into the shipping stage, but it does not promise that every carrier event will appear immediately. This is the point at which the waybill and Tracking & logistics section become the central records. Canceled means the parcel will not continue under that submission. Completed is the account’s completed workflow label; confirm the actual delivery situation before using any separate receipt-confirmation action.

3. Separate a static parcel status from a static tracking timeline

A parcel can remain marked Shipped while several logistics events appear beneath it. In that case, the workflow status is stable but tracking is still moving. Conversely, a waybill can be present while the Tracking & logistics section says that no events are available. Those are different situations and should be described differently to support.

Build a short timeline from the account: submission date, current parcel status, time of the newest visible logistics event and the date you checked. Copy the event wording exactly instead of paraphrasing it as “stuck” or “lost.” If an event names a location or operational step, preserve that text and a screenshot.

Do not infer a delivery date from the number of scans. Routes can involve export processing, carrier handoffs, customs and local delivery systems, and not every operational movement produces a customer-facing event. The page’s latest confirmed event is evidence; an assumed movement between events is not.

4. Verify the parcel details that can explain a delay

Check the recipient block for the destination country and address summary. If you notice an error after submission, document it and contact support promptly rather than assuming it can still be changed. Whether a correction is possible depends on the parcel’s actual stage and the parties handling it.

Review the shipping method and item list. A parcel containing several goods should show the goods associated with that package. Also compare estimated and final shipping information where the page provides it. The current details page can distinguish estimated freight and chargeable weight from the final figures confirmed after weigh-in.

Check parcel-level fees and site messages for an amount due or refund notice. LoloBuy’s current parcel-payment guidance says differences between estimated and actual shipping cost may be communicated through an in-site message. A parcel awaiting an account action should not be described as a carrier tracking failure.

5. Treat “no tracking events yet” as a description, not a verdict

The parcel interface explicitly supports an empty state reading “No tracking events yet.” That message confirms only that the page has no event to display at that moment. It does not establish loss, a customs hold, a failed label or a delivery estimate.

First confirm that the parcel is marked Shipped and that a waybill number is present. Save a dated screenshot of the empty timeline and the package details. Recheck the official account before opening multiple requests. If an external carrier page is identifiable from the selected method, compare the waybill there, but keep the LoloBuy parcel page as part of the evidence set.

When an event exists but has not changed, quote the newest event and its timestamp. A useful question is, “Can you confirm the current carrier or handoff stage for this waybill?” An unhelpful conclusion is, “The parcel is definitely lost.” Support can investigate a precise last-known record more effectively than an unsupported outcome.

6. Check site messages before opening a new conversation

LoloBuy uses in-site messages for order and parcel communication. Review unread messages, station notices and the parcel record before contacting support. A request for information, a billing adjustment or an operational notice may already explain why the visible parcel stage has not advanced.

The session interface supports messages, image uploads and an associated-goods reference. Use the parcel or relevant order as the associated record when possible. That context is more useful than starting with only a username or a cropped screenshot that omits the parcel number and event time.

Keep product feedback separate from parcel support. The public feedback form is designed for problems using the website or suggestions and can accept a screenshot and contact information. A parcel-status question belongs with the transaction-aware support or message channel where the package can be identified privately.

7. Send a support request that can be investigated

Use a compact factual structure: package number, waybill number, current parcel status, shipping method, newest tracking event and timestamp, destination country, and the specific question you want answered. State what you have already checked. Attach one full screenshot of Package Details and one of the logistics timeline if needed.

For example: “Package [private number] is marked Shipped. Waybill [private number] shows the latest event as [exact text] at [displayed time]. The destination is [country]. I checked Package Details and site messages on [date] and found no newer event. Please confirm the current carrier or whether you need information from me.”

Do not include card numbers, passwords, identity documents or unrelated account data. Do not send repeated messages that change the description. If support requests additional evidence, keep the reply in the same conversation so the package, timestamps and attachments remain together.

8. Know when an after-sales or claim path is separate

The current Package Details interface may show a protection-service section for eligible parcels. Its claim flow can request a loss type, affected goods, a description and supporting files. This is a separate, parcel-specific process; it is not the automatic next step for every unchanged tracking event.

Check whether protection is present and active for the parcel, read the displayed rules and use only the claim types actually offered in the account. Coverage, required evidence, filing periods and outcomes depend on those terms. A tracking gap alone does not prove eligibility or guarantee compensation.

If the parcel arrives damaged, keep the outer package, waybill, item photos and an unboxing record when available. If it has not arrived, preserve the tracking history and support conversation. Evidence should document what happened, not manufacture certainty about who is responsible.

Final LoloBuy parcel-status checklist

Confirm the correct package number and waybill. Read the parcel workflow status first, then the logistics timeline. Check the address, shipping method, item list, final weight or fee information and unread site messages. Record the latest event exactly and note when you checked it.

If the record still needs investigation, send one private, evidence-based support request linked to the parcel. Use a protection or claim flow only when it is available and applicable to that shipment. This approach cannot promise a faster scan or a particular outcome, but it replaces guesswork with the identifiers, dates and evidence needed to understand a LoloBuy parcel status that is not updating.
